principles: Pre-reg rev3.1 is the authority -- outcomes, common-cell denominators, single BH-FDR, and per-scenario-exploratory-only mirror sections 4/5/7/8 exactly.
Reuse, do not re-derive: import the driver's CONTRASTS + scenarioAppliesToArm + denominatorSetsFor so analysis denominators match the stamped records; only READ recorded outcomes (never re-score).

Honest about Node vs R: Node computes the verifiable parts (rates, Wilson CIs, a seeded cluster bootstrap respecting within-cell clustering, BH-FDR); the formal GLMM is emitted as glmm.R, not run in Node.
Every reported rate states its common-cell denominator; nothing is computed over a non-common cell set.
Fully deterministic + offline: synthetic section-7 fixtures of known rates/contrasts; seeded bootstrap reproducible.
drivers: Must match the pre-registered common-cell + outcome + FDR rules verbatim and operate only on recorded section-7 JSONL.
The contrast CI must respect within-cell repeat dependence (cluster bootstrap), since k repeats per cell are not independent.
Selfcheck must verify against KNOWN synthetic rates/contrasts with zero live-model calls and a non-vacuous negative control.

options.name: cluster-bootstrap-plus-glmm-r
pros: In-Node contrast CI (cluster bootstrap) is fully verifiable + deterministic
GLMM emitted as glmm.R = honest about the formal model running in R
Rates/Wilson CIs/BH-FDR all pure + testable against known fixtures
Reuses driver contrast defs so denominators are consistent
cons: Bootstrap CI is an approximation of the GLMM contrast (documented as a proxy)

options.name: pure-js-glmm
cons: A correct GLMM (Laplace/AGQ for binomial mixed models) is hard + unreliable in pure JS
Would be unverifiable + a likely source of silent statistical error -- violates the honesty principle

rationale: The pre-reg requires a GLMM for the primary contrast, but a correct binomial GLMM in pure JS is unreliable and unverifiable. The honest, testable design computes in Node only what Node can verify deterministically -- per-arm rates, Wilson 95pct CIs, BH-FDR, and a SEEDED CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP risk-difference CI that respects within-cell (k-repeat) dependence -- and emits a ready-to-run glmm.R (lme4::glmer primary ~ arm + (1|task)+(1|scenario)+(1|seed)) for the formal model, clearly labeled as the authority while the bootstrap is the in-Node proxy. UNKNOWN-1 resolved: the bootstrap resamples the COMMON-CELL clusters = distinct (task,scenario) pairs WITH ALL their k repeats (cluster bootstrap), so within-cell dependence is preserved; arms are paired within each resampled cell. UNKNOWN-2 resolved: per-scenario exploratory tests use the two-proportion z-test feeding ONE Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (Fisher-exact noted in a comment for very small cells); these are EXPLORATORY only, never the primary readout.

preMortem.scenario: Rates computed over the wrong denominator (not common-cell)
preMortem.trigger: Using each arm's own applicable cells instead of the intersection applicable to BOTH contrast arms
preMortem.consequence: Biased headline rates -- the exact denominator-bias the pre-reg warns against
preMortem.mitigation: denominatorSetsFor (driver-shared) decides membership; selfcheck asserts known common-cell counts for A4-vs-A2prime (all scenarios) vs A4-vs-A1 (excludes B4/B5/B10)

preMortem.trigger: Resampling individual runs instead of (task,scenario) clusters
preMortem.mitigation: Resample whole (task,scenario) clusters with their k repeats; selfcheck asserts a fixture where independent-run resampling would give a narrower CI than the cluster resampling

preMortem.trigger: Not applying the section-7 validity filter before counting
preMortem.mitigation: Filter excludes infraVoid + applicable=false BEFORE counting; task-failures kept; selfcheck asserts a fixture with void+N/A rows yields the same rates as the cleaned set

preMortem.trigger: Using Math.random or an unsalted RNG
preMortem.consequence: Non-reproducible CIs -> paper numbers cannot be regenerated
preMortem.mitigation: Seeded PRNG (same xmur3+mulberry32 as the driver); selfcheck asserts two runs with the same seed give byte-identical CI bounds
